study: Fong et al. 2015, Expository Reading and Writing Course (ERWC), WestEd i3 (QED)
eval_evidence: Evaluation by WestEd under a U.S. ED i3 Development grant; WestEd is the external evaluator, not the ERWC/CSU program developer.
developer_evidence: ERWC teacher PD (two-day summer session + PLCs + coaching) is part of the CSU ERWC program delivered through the school/district system; the publication does not show the developers/research team delivering the PD themselves.
cascade_evidence: Report focuses on the QED student-level course-enrollment contrast; it does not specify whether ERWC PD reached teachers via developer-direct trainers or a cascade/site-based model.
counterfactual_evidence: Comparison = matched grade-12 students in non-ERWC English classes (English 4, AP English Lit, world/other literature) -> BAU regular English courses, not an active alternative PD program.
coaching_evidence: Teacher professional-learning component listed as a two-day summer PD plus professional learning communities and coaching; coaching is mentioned as a support but no in-class coaching cycle frequency is given (light/periodic).
student_dose_evidence: ERWC is itself the students' grade-12 English course (a different curriculum), compared to other English courses; no add-on tutoring/pull-out/extra minutes beyond the regular English class.
maturity_evidence: Outcomes measured spring 2014; the report does not state whether the 56 ERWC teachers were in their first ERWC year or had prior years of ERWC experience.
